question: Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed Ibn Battuta to the post of the _________ in Delhi.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Qazi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1334, Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed Ibn Battuta as the Qazi (judge) of Delhi.
 
• Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan explorer and traveler, who is known for his extensive travels covering most of the Islamic world and beyond.
 
• As a Qazi, Ibn Battuta was responsible for administering justice according to Islamic law.
 
• Ibn Battuta's travelogue, "Rihla" (The Journey), provides a comprehensive account of his travels and experiences, including his time in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amalguzar:**

 
 
• An Amalguzar was a revenue officer responsible for collecting taxes from the peasants and managing revenue affairs in the region.
 
• The position was crucial for maintaining the financial stability of the empire.
 
 
 
• **Shiqdar:**
 
 
• A Shiqdar was an administrative officer in charge of a district or province, responsible for maintaining law and order and implementing the policies of the ruler.
 
• They played a significant role in the local administration and governance.
 
 
 
• **Kotwal:**
 
 
• A Kotwal was the chief police officer of a city, responsible for maintaining public order and safety.
 
• The Kotwal also supervised the markets and ensured the implementation of laws and regulations.
 
 
 
• **Ibn Battuta:**
 
 
• Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan explorer who is known for his extensive travels, which lasted for about 30 years.
 
• His travelogue, "Rihla," is one of the most important sources of information about the medieval Islamic world.
 
• During his travels, he visited North Africa, the Horn of Africa, West Africa, Southern Europe, Eastern Europe, the Middle East, the Indian subcontinent, Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and China.
 
• His appointment as Qazi in Delhi was a notable event in his life, providing valuable insights into the administration and culture of the Tughlaq dynasty.
